differences.text: The scroll position, not CSS anchor positioning, drives everything: the sliding bar is measured from the active link (top and height, transitioned), because anchor positioning is not in every Tier-1 engine (D-014), and the active heading is the last one whose top passed the activation line, recomputed from live positions on every scroll and on layout changes, so it is right on load and when scrolling up (mwg:scrollspy; scroll-target-group is Chromium only). A page that does not scroll at all keeps the first item active.

Links are native anchors in the outline's shadow root (in-page fragment links need no router, so the Link dependency is not used); a missing target is left to the browser. Headings are found by id in the outline's own tree, then the document.

Upstream is controlled through `activeId` + `onActiveIdChange`; here `activeId` set means controlled and `tct-active-change` reports every change. The other callbacks are events: tct-navigate-start and tct-navigate-end. Three new core events carry them (core/src/events).

Links are secondary text; the active one is primary text one weight heavier, with the 2px bar in the primary icon colour on a 2px track. Hover, keyboard focus and pressed use the tertiary action fills each paired with its own text role.

core.outline.notes: Guides: [mwg:scrollspy] (aria-current mirrored with the visual state; a position-based fallback because scroll-target-group is not available everywhere) [mwg:anchor-positioning-tab-underline] (the bar is decorative; measured position instead of anchor positioning) [mwg:accessibility] (nav landmark, one roving tab stop) [mwg:spatial-navigation] (arrow keys and Home/End).
